It starts small. A prompt you can't quite type.
So you press a key, and say it out loud.
And it's... just there. Cleaner than you said it.
Day one, it feels strange. Talking to your laptop. Day two, you forget. Day three, you catch yourself pressing the key before you've decided to.
By the end of the week, you talk to everything. Email. Code comments. That message you've been putting off.
You even start giving it instructions. Tucky, make this an email. And it does. In your voice.
That's the moment you can't go back.
Then one evening, you open the library. Every thought you spoke this week is sitting there. Searchable. And you wonder... if my thoughts are worth keeping...
So the next call, you let it listen. Live transcript. A guide that tracks what you've covered, and nudges the next question.
And when you hang up, the decisions and follow-ups are already written.
Weeks go by. Meetings, notes, a screen recording you narrated for a client. It all lands in one place, sorted by project.
So you ask it. What did we decide on pricing with Acme? And it answers. And shows you where it came from.
Every morning: what happened, what matters, what's next.
One last question. Where does all of this live? Here. On your Mac. No account. No cloud. No subscription.
It started with one key. Typing is overrated. Just talk.
